reasoning: Recent Alaska polling for the 2026 U.S. Senate race shows a very tight contest with a slight Democratic edge in the polling average but within the margin of error, so the race is effectively a toss-up with perhaps a D+1 to D+2 polling advantage. Structurally, however, Alaska remains an R+6 state by Cook PVI, so any Democratic lead in current polls should be treated as fragile and contingent, not as a durable partisan shift.

sources.name: New York Times interactive: Alaska U.S. Senate Election 2026 – Latest Polls
sources.details: New York Times interactive polling page summarizes recent Alaska Senate polls, including an Alaska Survey Research poll showing Mary Peltola 51% to Dan Sullivan 49% (Peltola +2) and a Data for Progress poll with Peltola +6 in a ranked-choice final round.

sources.name: Data for Progress
sources.details: Data for Progress poll of 605 likely Alaska voters finds Mary Peltola leading Dan Sullivan 47% to 41% in the first round and by 6 points in a ranked-choice final round.

sources.name: Alaska Survey Research
sources.details: Alaska Survey Research poll, as summarized in multiple outlets, finds Mary Peltola leading Dan Sullivan 50.8% to 49.2% in the ranked-choice final round (Peltola +1.6, usually rounded to +2).

sources.name: Siena College / New York Times (reported by Washington Examiner)
sources.details: Siena University/New York Times poll reported by Washington Examiner finds Dan Sullivan leading Mary Peltola 47% to 45%, within the margin of error, indicating a very tight race.

sources.name: Deseret (summarizing RealClearPolitics average)
sources.details: Deseret article notes that RealClearPolitics’ average for the Alaska Senate race shows Mary Peltola at 46.7% and Dan Sullivan at 46.3%, effectively a Peltola +0.4, and cites the latest Alaska Survey Research poll with Peltola up by 2 points.
sources.date_range: Not specified (article published August 17, 2026, summarizing recent polls)

sources.name: PollsMax forecast (reported by Alaska Story)
sources.details: PollsMax forecast, reported by Alaska Story, gives Dan Sullivan an 83.3% chance to win and projects he will defeat Mary Peltola by 5.8 percentage points in the Senate race.
sources.date_range: Not a poll; model snapshot as of July 20, 2026

sources.name: Washington Examiner (citing Cook Political Report toss-up rating)
sources.details: Washington Examiner article describes the Alaska Senate race as one of the most closely watched of 2026, citing multiple polls (including NYT/Siena and Alaska Survey Research) and noting that the Cook Political Report has rated the race a toss-up.
sources.date_range: Article dated August 18, 2026, summarizing recent polling

sources.name: Cook Political Report (rating, as reported)
sources.details: Cook Political Report is reported to rate the Alaska 2026 U.S. Senate race as a toss-up, reflecting no clear advantage for either party despite the state’s Republican lean.
sources.date_range: Rating current as of mid-2026 (article cited August 18, 2026)

sources.details: Official Alaska primary election summary report lists vote totals and turnout for the U.S. Senate all-party primary but does not provide any general-election margin or clear partisan advantage beyond identifying candidate affiliations.
